Consult Summary:
- Acute gastroenteritis is suspected (likely viral) in a patient with 3 days of watery diarrhea, left-lower abdominal cramps, weakness/feverish sensation, prior vomiting, and reduced appetite; conservative management with hydration, dietary adjustments, and activity modification planned, with follow-up in 3–4 days and stool testing if symptoms persist.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 3 days of loose, watery stools; six to seven bowel movements per day; associated left lower abdominal cramp-like pain; feel weak and shaky; feverish sensation noted at onset.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms began ~3 days ago; initially with vomiting which has since resolved; diarrhea and cramps persist; appetite decreased; able to hold fluids.
- Exposures/triggers: Recent takeaway meal ~4 days ago (Chinese restaurant); no other dietary triggers reported.
- Associated symptoms: No blood in stools or vomit; no night sweats; no persistent vomiting currently; moderate reduced appetite; able to maintain some fluids; no noted urinary symptoms.
- Symptoms in context: Affected daily activities; still attending work but finds it difficult.
- Past Medical History: Asthma, managed with inhaler; asthma described as well-controlled.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Medications: Asthma inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); no other medications.
- Social History: Non-smoker; does not drink alcohol; occupation: accountant; lives with wife and two children; currently going to work though symptoms impede functioning.
- Family History: Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma, well-controlled on inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis, likely viral (possible bacterial etiology discussed)
  - Plan:
    - Hydration: encourage continued fluid intake; use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) to replenish fluids/electrolytes.
    - Diet: maintain fluids with light foods as tolerated (soups, smoothies, liquid foods); avoid dehydration.
    - Medications: Paracetamol 2 tablets, up to 4 times daily, for the first few days for fever/weakness (route not documented; dose per tablet not specified).
    - Activity: advise rest and take 2–3 days off work to allow infection to clear.
    - Antibiotics: not indicated at this time.
    - Follow-up: re-evaluate in 3–4 days if symptoms have not improved; if symptoms persist or worsen, consider further evaluation including stool sample testing and additional investigations as needed.
    - Other considerations: discuss potential alternative diagnoses if symptoms do not improve with conservative management.
